summary: Kickoff standup to align on VPC peering, staging network, security needs (SOC2/audit logs), and performance benchmarks. Pilot success criteria and perf benchmarks
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, apologies for starting a minute late. This is Maya from Redwood, I run the AE on this account. Carlos and Evan are with me.
[00:07] Lena Park: Thanks Maya, hi all, Lena here. We just want to make sure we get the VPC details pinned down today and figure out staging runbook.
[00:13] Carlos Ortega: Great, quick agenda — network intake, security checklist, perf benchmark plan, and then next steps. Sound good?
[00:18] Omar Ruiz: Yeah that's perfect. We're mostly GCP right now, but we have a hybrid footprint — some on-prem for regulated workloads. We need to understand if Redwood Private is feasible or if we do Dedicated in our account.
[00:27] Evan Patel: Right, so short answer: Private gives you full VPC control and VPC peering, Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood cloud with isolated tenancy but not full VPC. We'll walk through network flows and what we need for peering.
[00:37] Devon Miles: Quick note, our SREs prefer minimizing cross-region egress; most traffic will stay in us-central1.
[00:41] Maya Chen: Good callout. On peering, the things we need from you: staging VPC CIDR, desired subnets for public egress, and whether you need static egress IPs or a proxy. We'll send the doc that shows options.
[00:52] Priya Nair: Also need to confirm encryption at rest and KMS integration — we have an HSM-backed KMS requirement for some workloads.
[00:58] Evan Patel: We support customer KMS for Private and Dedicated via our KMS integration — typically we surface a vault/KMS key for model artifacts and logs. We'll note that as an item.
[01:06] Speaker 1: (inaudible) sorry, did you say signing key rotation cadence?
[01:09] Evan Patel: Yes, rotation is supported; we document recommended cadence.
[01:12] Carlos Ortega: I'll put that under the security checklist.
[01:15] Lena Park: Show us the network topology you expect for peering — i.e. do we NAT outbound traffic or do you prefer we route via a private interconnect?
[01:22] Maya Chen: Two common patterns: 1) VPC peering with NAT for outbound egress, or 2) PrivateLink-style where the customer owns the egress and requests allowlist of Redwood endpoint IPs. For Private deployments we can support direct routing inside the VPC.
[01:36] Omar Ruiz: For onboarding speed, peering plus NAT is probably easiest. But we need static egress IPs for some third-party services. How do we get static IPs?
[01:44] Evan Patel: For static egress we usually front with a NAT gateway or an egress proxy in your environment. If you need Redwood-provided static egress, that'll be part of the Dedicated network plan, and we'll map our egress pool to your allowlist. There was some transcription note earlier where KV cache got transcribed as K V cash, sorry for that in the doc.
[02:00] Lena Park: Ha, yes I saw that in the shared notes. Also regarding pilot success, we need to measure 95th percentile latency under 1s for the 512-token generation path and cost per 1k tokens under our budget threshold.
[02:12] Evan Patel: Understood. We'll capture the perf tests — initial script will emulate your typical prompt mix. We'll send a benchmark plan.
[02:18] Maya Chen: On timelines, are you aiming to have a staging pilot by end of month?
[02:22] Lena Park: Ideally yes, but depends on how fast we can provision the staging VPC and share subnets.
[02:26] Omar Ruiz: We have a networking change window next Wednesday, so if we can get the runbook before Monday we can likely provision by Friday.
[02:33] Maya Chen: Great — we'll get the runbook by Thursday COB.
[02:37] Priya Nair: On audit logs — we need per-request logs with user token attribution and request/response hashes for PII redaction traceability. Is that available?
[02:46] Evan Patel: We provide request-level logs for Private and Dedicated; Hosted can provide obfuscated logs for privacy. For Private, you can export full audit trails to your SIEM — timestamps, request metadata, model version, latency, token counts. Full response bodies are opt-in due to PII.
[03:02] Devon Miles: And retention options? We need 12 months for some teams.
[03:06] Carlos Ortega: We can configure log retention for Private deployments up to 24 months if required — we'll include retention options in the runbook.
[03:12] Speaker 2: (overlap) so, uh, about SSO — we use Okta, SAML is required.
[03:16] Maya Chen: Okta SAML is supported, and we have SSO runbook and metadata exchange steps. We'll coordinate with your identity team.
[03:22] Lena Park: We'll need RBAC mapping — teams want dev vs prod access separation.
[03:26] Evan Patel: We support RBAC at route/model level and token scoping — we'll provide role examples in the runbook.
[03:31] Omar Ruiz: One more network nuance: our on-prem segment can't directly peer to cloud — we'd tunnel to GCP. Can Redwood support hybrid routing where we proxy requests through a central staging host?
[03:41] Evan Patel: Yes, we often see customers use a proxy/bastion to bridge on-prem to the staging VPC. It's an extra hop but acceptable for checks; for low latency production we'd recommend colocating inference in-region via Private or Dedicated.
[03:54] Lena Park: Ok noted. Switching gear — cost controls. How do we instrument token-level spend and set alarms during pilot?
[04:00] Carlos Ortega: On the Console we expose token-level breakdowns per API key and per model/route. We can set budget alerts and rate limits. For a pilot we'll set a conservative quota and a notification schedule.
[04:10] Devon Miles: Can we restrict model families? We don't want experimental models rolling out without approval.
[04:14] Evan Patel: Absolutely — model pinning is supported. You can pin to a model version and block access to other catalog entries.
[04:19] Speaker 3: (soft) there was a question on quantization — do you support int8?
[04:22] Evan Patel: Yes, runtime supports common quantization profiles including int8 and int4 in some cases. We'll recommend profiles based on your perf vs quality tolerance.
[04:29] Lena Park: We'll want a quick A/B quality check on any quantized profile before we switch.
[04:33] Evan Patel: Totally, that's part of Optimize — we can run evals on your prompt set and provide quality delta metrics.
[04:39] Maya Chen: Okay, quick recap and assignments: Evan will draft perf script and runbook; I'll send VPC peering checklist and security docs; Carlos will set up a Console walkthrough and budget alert template. Omar and Devon will provision staging VPC details and Priya will send SOC2 scope. Does that align?
[04:58] Omar Ruiz: Yep aligns. I'll put provisioning in my backlog and aim to share CIDRs by the 25th.
[05:03] Priya Nair: I'll extract the list of audit fields and share by Friday next week.
[05:07] Lena Park: One more thing — for compliance we need a data flow diagram. Can Redwood provide a template?
[05:12] Carlos Ortega: Yes I'll attach a data flow template and example diagrams from previous Private deployments.
[05:18] Maya Chen: Cool. Are there any blockers we haven't surfaced?
[05:22] Devon Miles: Not yet, just need the runbook and the perf window.
[05:26] [09:12] Speaker 1: (laughter) small time jump in transcript, looks like conference dropped a bit
[05:30] Maya Chen: Haha, okay. Last housekeeping — we'll use the shared drive link in the calendar invite for artifacts. Expect the runbook, network checklist, and benchmark script links by Thursday.
[05:39] Lena Park: Thanks, that works. We'll block time for the perf session once Evan shares his availability.
[05:45] Carlos Ortega: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the Console walkthrough and include the data flow template.
[05:50] Priya Nair: Thanks all.
[05:52] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll talk soon. Bye.
[05:55] Transcript notes: occasional transcription noise; speaker labels may be imperfect. Some technical terms transcribed (KV cache, K V cash) incorrectly in auto notes — corrected in action items.
